question: The area of a square is 1296 cm² and the radius of a circle is (7)/(6) of the length of a side of the square. What is the ratio of the perimeter of the square and the circumference of the circle? [Use π = (22)/(7)]
solution:
**Given:**

Area of Square = 1296 cm²

Radius of circle = (7)/(6) of the length of a side of the square

**Concept Used:**

Area of Square = Side²

Perimeter of Square = 4 × Side

Circumference of Circle = 2pi r

**Calculation:**

Area of Square = Side² = 1296

Side = sqrt{1296} = 36 cm

Now, Radius of circle = (7)/(6)times 36 = 42 cm

Perimeter of Square = 4 × Side

Perimeter of Square = 4 × 36 = 144 cm

Circumference of circle = 2pi r

Circumference of circle = 2times (22)/(7)times 42=44times 6 = 264 cm

Ratio of Perimeter and Circumference = (144)/(264)=(6)/(11) = 6 : 11

**Hence, the ratio of the perimeter of square and circumference of circle is 6 : 11.**
